evals.prompt: Morgan at Northwind emailed asking to push the design review two weeks so their content team can finish the copy. Update the Northwind website redesign project.
evals.expected_output: Reads the snapshot and the email, asks whether the client agreed to a new Committed date or this is a re-plan, previews the schedule change and shows conflicts, applies only after confirmation, and records the source and reason.
followups: The client agreed to the new date. Go ahead.
assertions: Reads the project with get_project before proposing changes
Asks whether this is approved or changes what the client was promised before moving dates
Calls preview_schedule_change before changing a date
Makes no change before the person confirms
After the client agreed, changes the Design review milestone's Committed date (apply_bulk_change with the Committed basis), not only its working date
Records where the change came from (the email) in a reason or comment
Makes no more than two failed tool calls from wrong parameter names

evals.prompt: Notes from today's Northwind check-in, can you update the project? - homepage mockup v2 approved - Sam is out next week, Lee covers the QA plan - the inventory API work is probably slipping, maybe a week
evals.expected_output: Proposes accepting the homepage mockup, an owner change for the QA plan task that needs its own yes, and treats the vague API slip as a risk or comment rather than a date change; leaves unmentioned items alone.
assertions: Proposes marking the homepage mockup accepted
Proposes moving the QA plan task to Lee and asks for confirmation of the owner change
Does not move any date for the vague API slip; treats it as a risk or comment
Leaves items the notes don't mention unchanged
Makes changes only after approval

evals.prompt: The client says the product data file will arrive {{data_file_new_date}} instead of {{data_file_date}}. Their email is in Penroe. Review what this affects and propose changes to the Northwind catalog migration project.
evals.expected_output: Reads the email and the plan, treats the new arrival date as information rather than an approved re-plan, and asks before proposing date changes. After the person asks for a re-plan, previews both moves, reports that moving Data testing leaves the Testing sign-off milestone in conflict, and asks for a separate decision on it. On approval, moves only the data file and Data testing working dates, leaves the milestone and every Committed date alone, records the email as the source, and drafts a client update that raises the milestone decision without sending it.
followups: Yes. Propose moving the data handoff to {{data_file_new_date}} and testing to {{testing_new_end_date}}. The client hasn't agreed to change any committed dates.
Yes, apply those two changes. Leave the milestone unchanged for now and draft a client update that raises the milestone decision.
assertions: Reads the project with get_project and the client's email before proposing changes
On the first turn, treats the new arrival date as information rather than an approved change, and asks before re-planning; makes no change
Calls preview_schedule_change for the data file and Data testing dates before saving either
Reports that the new Data testing end date would leave the Testing sign-off milestone in conflict, and asks for a decision on it instead of moving it
Changes nothing before the person approves the two changes

After approval, the data file's due date and Data testing's end date are the two dates the person approved (data_file_new_date and testing_new_end_date in workspace.json); the Testing sign-off milestone and every other date are unchanged
Changes no Committed date (no apply_bulk_change with the committed basis)
Records the client's email as the source or reason of the change
Drafts a client update that gives the new testing date, raises the milestone decision and says the existing commitment is unchanged, and does not claim to have sent it
Makes no more than two failed tool calls from wrong parameter names

should_not_trigger: What's the status of the Northwind website redesign?
